The amplitude is the coefficient in front of the cosine:
\[
A=0.020\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: For \(y(x,t)=A\cos(6x-18t)\), is the wave moving left or right?
questions.answer: The form \(kx-\omega t\) represents a wave moving to the right.

questions.prompt: A wave is described by \(y(x,t)=0.040\cos(8x-32t+\pi/3)\). Find the phase difference between two points separated by \(0.25\,\mathrm{m}\) at the same instant.
questions.answer:
At one instant the phase difference over a separation \(\Delta x\) is
\[
\Delta\phi=k\Delta x=(8)(0.25)=2.0\,\mathrm{rad}
\]

questions.prompt: A pulse shape at \(t=0\) is \(y(x,0)=g(x)\). Write expressions for the same pulse moving right and left with speed \(v_w\).
questions.answer:
A right-moving pulse is
\[
y(x,t)=g(x-v_w t)
\]
and a left-moving pulse is
\[
y(x,t)=g(x+v_w t)
\]

questions.prompt: For \(y(x,t)=A\cos(kx-\omega t+\phi)\), derive the equation relating \(x\) and \(t\) for a fixed phase point and hence show that the phase speed is constant.
questions.answer:
A fixed phase point satisfies
\[
kx-\omega t+\phi=\text{constant}
\]
Differentiate with respect to time:
\[
k\frac{dx}{dt}-\omega=0
\]
so
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{\omega}{k}
\]
Since \(\omega\) and \(k\) are constants for this wave, the phase speed is constant:
\[
v_w=\frac{\omega}{k}
\]

questions.prompt: A sensor at \(x=0\) records \(y(0,t)=A\cos(\omega t)\). A second sensor at \(x=d\) records the same oscillation delayed by a time \(\tau\). Build a right-moving wave equation consistent with these observations and express \(k\) and \(v_w\) in terms of \(\omega\), \(d\), and \(\tau\).
questions.answer:
A right-moving wave can be written as
\[
y(x,t)=A\cos(kx-\omega t+\phi)
\]
At \(x=0\), the sensor records \(A\cos(\omega t)\). Since cosine is even, one convenient equivalent form is
\[
y(x,t)=A\cos(\omega t-kx)
\]
At \(x=d\), the second sensor is delayed by \(\tau\), so it records
\[
y(d,t)=A\cos\!\bigl(\omega(t-\tau)\bigr)=A\cos(\omega t-\omega\tau)
\]
Match the phases:
\[
kd=\omega\tau
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
k=\frac{\omega\tau}{d}
\]
Then
\[
v_w=\frac{\omega}{k}=\frac{d}{\tau}
\]
So a consistent right-moving wave is
\[
y(x,t)=A\cos\!\left(\omega t-\frac{\omega\tau}{d}x\right)
\]
